chapter: This Is Your Life and film work
title: How her family set up the surprise
summary: Friends and family in Lake Charles, with her manager, arranged the show and told her she would only sing Let's Start the New Year Right.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: So they got in touch with Mr. Gastel', my manager, and told him what they wanted. Well, he knew the whole story. My family knew the whole story, and my little sister Vida, who

used to travel with me, I told you about her. Vida was instrumental, and another friend who has gone on also. Vida has gone on, of course, and this friend Eugenia. Well, they got together and got all these facts, and we have a darling little friend back in Louisiana, Mary -- what's her name? Mary Burn Elliott. And also Rosa Hart from Lake Charles, who has gone on. But Rosa Hart was very, very strong and very instrumental in keeping the little theater going in Lake Charles, you know.

But anyway, anything theatrical and anybody theatrical she was with it and for it. She was just a marvelous person and Mary Burn Elliott and her family were just tremendous. So they knew all of this was going on, and they did the works of getting this thing, putting it in action. Unbeknownst to me, you know, and I absolutely had no idea, really. Because I've had people ask me, "You mean to tell me you didn't know?" I say no, I did not know. I had seen the show, you know, but I -- the way it was put to me, and they were just wonderful in doing it. They said, "We want you to do a number on the show," and the song was, "Let's Start the New Year Right, 12:00 O'Clock Tonight." They said, "That's what we want you to do. We want you to do the show and --," Gilda Gray, that's the woman's name, the woman whose -- I don't know if she's gone on now or not. Gilda Gray? She was a dancer.
I know the name but I don't remember her.

Gilda was a dancer, and this was what they told me, said, "We want you to do -- we're going to do Gilda Gray's life and we want you to do a number to bring her on, you know, and we want you to do, "Let's Start the New Year Right." Well, I didn't know, "Let's Start the New Year Right." I didn't even know it, but I learned it, and I think I even forgot some of the words that night, I was so excited.

I had no idea that this was going to happen, and funny, you know, this was on New Years night. It was on New Years night, now, and I was so excited. Well, I was excited over the idea that I was going to do this, becuase it was the first time on national TV, you know. And this was the thing that I was really excited over, the fact that I was going to do this on national TV. And when I -- after the thing was all over -- before it was all over, it was revealed that they had set everything up in Lake Charles, my home. They had set a screen up. They had made arrangements with the Chamber of Commerce, the Mayor and everybody in Lake Charles were watching this. It was all set up there on NBC. And they tried to get my parents to come out, but they were not well enough to come, you know. My mother was -- she wasn't ill at the time too, but my dad had had a stroke, and he was, you know -- and she really wanted to be there. She wouldn't leave him, and I wouldn't have wanted her to, you know.
